transcript.about: Oppose. Solar geoengineering is shallow ecology at its purest: it asks how to cool the planet without asking why industrial societies heat it. The work never addressed this technology, but by analogy, funding it signals that consumption and growth may stay untouched. The deep question comes first. Technical fixes that postpone it make the problem worse.

interviews.author: stewart-brand
interviews.reaction: Solar geoengineering research should go ahead. A technology should be judged by its measured effects on the climate, and only research produces those measurements. Shared rules can govern the research, and it works as a backup alongside nuclear power and dense cities, not instead of emission cuts.

interviews.author: hans-jonas
interviews.reaction: Opposed, reasoning by analogy. When action can alter planetary conditions of life, the bad prognosis outweighs the good. Solar geoengineering cannot be tested without being deployed, research builds momentum toward use, and future generations become the experiment, so restraint is the duty.

interviews.author: naomi-klein
interviews.reaction: Solar geoengineering research is a fix that leaves the fossil economy and its profits untouched. It builds pressure toward deployment and puts drought risks on the poorest regions. The answer is fast, fair emission cuts that change the system.

interviews.author: bjorn-lomborg
interviews.reaction: Research should go ahead because it is cheap and fills a gap in knowledge. Studying solar geoengineering shows its costs, risks and benefits next to those of deep emission cuts, so money can go first to where it does the most good.

interviews.author: bruno-latour
interviews.reaction: Opposed as framed. Solar geoengineering treats a reacting Earth as an object to steer from outside, and once built a sunshade demands centuries of care. Research is already a political choice, so those affected, human and not, must be assembled before it begins.

interviews.author: vandana-shiva
interviews.reaction: Solar geoengineering research turns a monoculture of the mind into a monoculture of the sky. One laboratory science would set the climate for peasants and forest communities who were never asked, leave the fossil-driven maldevelopment behind the crisis untouched, and risk enclosing the atmospheric commons.

interviews.author: amitav-ghosh
interviews.reaction: Oppose, reasoning by analogy. Solar geoengineering extends the logic of colonial terraforming into the sky. It treats Earth as an inert resource to be managed. A few powerful states would decide the climate for peoples who were never asked.

interviews.author: erik-swyngedouw
interviews.reaction: Solar geoengineering research turns climate into a thermostat run by experts, which depoliticises it. The economic order that produces emissions stays outside debate. Apocalyptic emergency framing builds consensus and pushes aside the political choice between different worlds.

interviews.author: jason-hickel
interviews.reaction: Opposed, by analogy. Solar geoengineering works like a promise that lets rich economies keep growing when they should be cutting energy and material use. Decoupling has not happened fast enough, so the answer is less throughput in the North, not dimming the sky over the South.

interviews.author: pope-francis
interviews.reaction: Solar geoengineering research extends the technocratic paradigm. It treats a moral and social crisis as a technical problem and leaves the throwaway culture untouched. It also shifts the risks onto the poor. Ecological conversion and cutting emissions must come first.

interviews.author: arne-naess
interviews.reaction: Solar geoengineering is shallow ecology. It treats symptoms and leaves untouched the question of why industrial societies overheat the planet. Research signals that consumption and growth can continue. The deep questioning has to come first, together with lives that are simple in means and rich in ends.

interviews.author: baird-callicott
interviews.reaction: Solar geoengineering research should not go ahead. It treats the whole biotic community as an instrument tuned for human comfort. The land ethic judges actions by whether they preserve that community's integrity and stability, and cost ledgers or human-only governance leave out its other members.

interviews.author: murray-bookchin
interviews.reaction: Solar geoengineering research should not go ahead. Ecological crises come from social hierarchy, and a planetary thermostat run by states and firms extends the domination of nature. No directly democratic assembly could govern it.

interviews.author: timothy-morton
interviews.reaction: Global warming is a hyperobject that everyone is already inside, so no one stands outside the sky to steer it. Research that promises a planetary thermostat repeats the picture of Nature as a thing apart. Inquiry carried out as entangled participants is less objectionable.

interviews.author: james-lovelock
interviews.reaction: Research should go ahead, but deployment should not. The Earth regulates itself through feedbacks that are poorly understood. Since sustainable development is too late, a planned retreat needs that knowledge before an emergency forces a blind planetary gamble.

interviews.author: ted-nordhaus
interviews.reaction: Research should go ahead, under shared rules that give the most exposed countries a voice. Banning study is one more politics of limits. Knowledge widens options, while cheap clean energy and decarbonisation remain the main task. The record does not address geoengineering directly, so this is argued by analogy.

interviews.author: andreas-malm
interviews.reaction: Solar geoengineering research should not go ahead. Warming comes from fossil capital, an owning class that chose coal to control labour. Dimming the sun leaves that capital burning and puts off the fight over who owns energy. Funding belongs to dismantling the fossil economy.

interviews.author: william-nordhaus
interviews.reaction: Research should go ahead as insurance against catastrophic climate damages, but not deployment. Solar geoengineering leaves acidification untouched and carries risks not yet priced, so it cannot replace a carbon price rising along an optimal path.

interviews.author: gunther-anders
interviews.reaction: Solar geoengineering widens the Promethean gap between what can be made and what can be imagined or felt. Research is not neutral: once the means exist, they press toward use, and human foresight cannot follow a sunshade for the whole planet.

interviews.author: elinor-ostrom
interviews.reaction: Solar geoengineering research can proceed only conditionally, as governance of a shared sky. Those affected must help make, monitor and enforce the rules through nested, polycentric institutions, not leave the decision to one state, firm or lab. This is reasoned by analogy.

interviews.author: bill-mckibben
interviews.reaction: Nature as a world apart has already ended, and dimming the sun would turn that accident into deliberate management of the sky. On a tougher planet, the task is to stop burning fossil fuels and build smaller, sturdier communities, not more centralised planetary control.

interviews.author: isabelle-stengers
interviews.reaction: Opposed. Solar geoengineering research assumes Gaia can be steered, but she intrudes and is indifferent to human reasons. Emergency research builds pressure toward deployment. Decisions must slow down until those affected, human or not, can object before the agenda is set.

interviews.author: jacques-ellul
interviews.reaction: Opposed, by analogy since the work predates geoengineering. A technical fix for the damage of technique is announced with its benefits and silent about its costs. Research builds experts, budgets and institutions that push toward use, and what can be done gets done.

interviews.author: pascal-bruckner
interviews.reaction: Research should go ahead. Refusing to study a possible remedy turns ecology into a morality of penance and fear. Ignorance is itself a risk, and human ingenuity, not repentance, offers protection, especially to the poor.

interviews.author: carolyn-merchant
interviews.reaction: Solar geoengineering research carries forward the mechanistic image of the earth as a machine to be controlled, the same image that once licensed mining. A partnership ethic puts emission cuts first and treats the earth's processes as having needs of their own.

interviews.author: jean-baptiste-fressoz
interviews.reaction: Energy sources have piled up and never replaced one another, and industry's dangers were known and accepted at every step. By analogy, solar geoengineering would add one more technical layer on top of fossil fuels and give coal and oil a longer life.
